profile: shared behavioral scenarios; Linux low-level bindings and qualified public SDK adapters

steps: Move a blocking client into an owned controller task
Abandon the controller's receive while accepted native work remains in flight
Join owned work and explicit close while keeping the controller responsive
Recover the same receipt from a fresh client
scenarios.limits: Rust and Ruby initial public APIs are blocking. Rust abandons an application's receive; Ruby kills its caller thread. Native work remains owned through close. Neither claims an executor adapter or interruption of native work. Rust compile-fail cases separately qualify exclusive access and consumed-handle rejection; Ruby rejects concurrent work at runtime. C/C++ use an owned blocking task; deferred POSIX cancellation is masked in SDK calls and asynchronous thread cancellation is unsupported. C rejects overlapping and closed access; C++ ownership types reject copies. Erlang/Elixir use a supervised coordinator and an owned native-port worker; cancelled callers/tasks keep admitted work busy and join through close. Dead unpublished reservations can be reclaimed. Original native shutdown acknowledgement and successful child exit prove cleanup.

steps: Install all public SDK/example/native artifacts outside the checkout
Run each language's documented counter CLI against a foreign-language requester
Restart the requester before its recorded reply and query result
Read original typed IPC with an independent consumer after closing both runners
scenarios.limits: A ten-edge ring covers every public target in both roles, not all 100 ordered pairs. Counter paths run installed language CLIs; Table/query paths reuse public proof adapters around installed example handlers. Three query rows cover null, signed extremes and values above 2^53; the separate per-SDK schedule covers six-segment streaming and authority/recovery failures. Linux x86_64 and pinned Nix native closures only.

steps: Install public SDK, examples and native artifacts in a clean consumer outside the checkout
Fail persistence and confirmation hooks for every mutation purpose
Stop without rerunning the handler and recover exact accepted bytes after host/node/store loss
Resume the requester from durable waiting state and verify its full-width reply
Read bounded Table pages and retained points, then consume original complete-result IPC after runner disposal
Revoke access during result reading and preserve retirement/read/ownership errors
scenarios.limits: Python 3.13 wheels Node 24 tarballs, Rust 1.95 crates and Ruby 3.4 gems on Linux with Nix-linked native artifacts; one owned worker/port, serial handlers, bounded native I/O and query workspace. Python injects allocation loss at its real C response wrapper; Node separately injects a retained confirmation in the runner unit proof and loss at its real raw port response parser. Rust checks borrowed scopes, panics under both policies and stop/join. Optional PyArrow 23, Arrow JavaScript 21.2 and Arrow Rust 59 consume owned segments separately. Ruby checks thread/fiber scopes, exceptions under both policies and caller interruption/join. It exposes owned IPC decoded independently with PyArrow, with no selected Ruby Arrow adapter. C/C++ add installed pkg-config artifacts, explicit C ownership, typed C++ wrappers, real C11/C++17 example binaries, retained scopes and stop/join on an 8 MiB worker. The shared controller drives C callbacks/direct runner and typed C++ handlers separately; original IPC is independently decoded with PyArrow, with no selected Arrow C/C++ adapter. Java 21 JARs add typed records/interfaces, BigInteger application values, bounded future publication, cancellation/stop/join, callback exceptions and Error failures, scoped access and original IPC after disposal. Java selects no optional Arrow adapter; independent PyArrow decoding is included. .NET 8 NuGet packages add typed synchronous handlers, async-void rejection, cancellation tokens with joined native cleanup, full-width nullable values and owned original IPC independently decoded with PyArrow; no optional .NET Arrow adapter is selected. Both BEAM APIs add typed records/structs, behaviours, supervised bounded ports, persistence/confirmation gates, scoped reentry guards, caller kill/stop/join, retained Tables and owned IPC independently decoded with PyArrow. A shared Erlang controller drives each public language adapter and installed native-language examples. No BEAM Arrow adapter is selected. The separate public-language-ring scenario qualifies every target in both roles.

steps: Require explicit query opt-in and start a typed native plan from an authenticated call
Persist every control/capture/receive proposal before dispatch
Lose an accepted staging response and retry the exact signed bytes
Restart both workers, authority and disk provider after a segment seal
Verify complete provenance and decode copied IPC after native disposal
Read the same result through the native port and reject stale scope and revoked access
scenarios.limits: Explicit growing C/port handles on disk Ursula with 64 resident pages, one 1 MiB workspace per query-enabled handle and 8192-byte segment bounds. Public SDK runners and optional Arrow adapters have separate qualification.

steps: Probe native operation support and prepare explicit v3 operations
Admit a full-width principal's request and lose the response
Restart the node/provider and retry opaque bytes from a fresh host without its seed
Reject malformed read/receipt responses without inventing a mutation rejection
Revoke access before both reads and historical receipt recovery
scenarios.limits: Qualifies the explicit raw ABI and shared signature/operation fixtures, not a public SDK handler runner or a growing Station foreign ABI.
